hints: Use the generalized binomial expansion of $(1+u)^{-3/2}$ with $u=-2x$, retaining terms through $x^2$.
Compute each sign and coefficient before multiplying by the outer factor $6-x$.
In the product retain every contribution up to $x^2$, collect like powers, and discard higher powers.
walkthrough:
Use the binomial series expansion $(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \dots$ with $u = -2x$ and $n = -\dfrac{3}{2}$:
$$(1 - 2x)^{-3/2} = 1 + \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)(-2x) + \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{5}{2}\right)}{2}(-2x)^2 + \dots$$

Calculate the coefficients of each power of $x$:
$$\text{Linear term: } \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)(-2x) = 3x$$
$$\text{Quadratic term coefficient: } \dfrac{15/4}{2} = \dfrac{15}{8}$$
$$\dfrac{15}{8}(-2x)^2 = \dfrac{15}{8}(4x^2) = \dfrac{60}{8}x^2 = \dfrac{15}{2}x^2$$
$$(1 - 2x)^{-3/2} = 1 + 3x + \dfrac{15}{2}x^2 + \dots$$

Multiply the expansion by $(6 - x)$:
$$(6 - x)\left(1 + 3x + \dfrac{15}{2}x^2\right) = 6\left(1 + 3x + \dfrac{15}{2}x^2\right) - x\left(1 + 3x + \dfrac{15}{2}x^2\right)$$
$$= 6 + 18x + 6\left(\dfrac{15}{2}\right)x^2 - x - 3x^2 - \dots$$
$$6\left(\dfrac{15}{2}\right)x^2 = 3(15)x^2 = 45x^2$$

Combine like powers of $x$ up to $x^2$:
$$\text{Constant: } 6$$
$$\text{Term in } x: 18x - x = 17x$$
$$\text{Term in } x^2: 45x^2 - 3x^2 = 42x^2$$
$$= 6 + 17x + 42x^2$$

hints: A generalized binomial expansion of $(1+u)^n$ is valid for $|u|<1$.
Here $u=-2x$, so apply the condition to $|-2x|$.
Solve for $x$ and state an open interval, since equality is not included.
walkthrough:
State the convergence condition for the infinite binomial expansion $(1 + u)^n$ where $n \notin \mathbb{N}$:
$$|u| < 1$$

Substitute $u = -2x$ into the condition and simplify:
$$|-2x| < 1$$
$$2|x| < 1$$
$$|x| < \dfrac{1}{2} \quad \left(\text{or } -\dfrac{1}{2} < x < \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$$
